facts.label: Past perfect
facts.sub: Ação mais antiga: had + particípio. Ação depois: passado simples. By the time I arrived, it had started. Pergunta: Had you…?

facts.label: Quando / até que
facts.sub: By the time liga duas ações no passado. A primeira, mais antiga, usa had + particípio: By the time I arrived, the film had started. A segunda usa o passado simples e fica depois da vírgula ou antes.

facts.label: Quando
facts.sub: When também mostra qual ação veio antes: When I looked at my phone, I saw that you had sent a message. A ação com had foi a primeira; a do passado simples, a segunda.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: In “By the time I arrived, it had started”, the film started first.
We form the past perfect with was + participle.
“When I looked, he had left” means he left before I looked.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: In “By the time I arrived, it had started”, the film started first. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We form the past perfect with was + participle. → Falso (We use had + participle.)
“When I looked, he had left” means he left before I looked. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A late evening at the cinema · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cold Friday evening in the centre of London. Crowds walk past the bright lights of Leicester Square. Nell has been running through the streets for twenty minutes. Her friend Paulo is waiting near the entrance. They planned to see a new film together tonight. Nell wants to explain what had already happened.

“By the time I reached the cinema in Leicester Square, the film had already started.” says Nell. “I know, sorry. By the time I left work, the traffic had become terrible.” says Paulo. “Don’t worry. When I looked at my phone, I saw that you had sent a message.” says Nell.
